problems.title: An inscribed angle from three equally spaced arguments
problems.question: A=(cosα,sinα),B=(cos2α,sin2α),C=(cos3α,sin3α). Which listed α gives greatest angle120°?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: For the listed0<α<180°, AB=BC and angle ABC=180°−α.
steps: It subtends the arc AC not containing B, of measure360°−2α.

problems.title: Match ranges of four sine expressions
problems.question: Which two have equal ranges: a=sinx+1,b=2sinx,c=sinx−|sinx|,d=sinx+|sinx|?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: The ranges are respectively[0,2],[−2,2],[−2,0],[0,2].
steps: For t≤0,t+|t|=0; for t≥0 it is2t.
Thus a and d both attain exactly[0,2].

problems.title: Order two inverse angles and a first root
problems.question: a=arcsin(−.5),b=arccos(−.5),c is the least positive root of sin2x=0. Order them.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Principal values give a=−π/6,b=2π/3; roots of sin2x=0 are x=kπ/2.
steps: Thus c=π/2, between a and b.

problems.title: An angle with a projected line
problems.question: AO is perpendicular to a plane containing B,C; angle ABC=45° and cosABO=√6/3. Find cosOBC.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: cosABC=cosABO·cosOBC by orthogonal projection.
steps: The required cosine is(√2/2)/(√6/3).

problems.title: A hexagonal section of a regular prism
problems.question: All edges of a regular hexagonal prism are1. Find the section through A,F,C₁.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: The section also contains D₁ and meets BB₁,EE₁ at their midpoints. Its projection is the full regular hexagonal base.
steps: Opposite base edges AF,CD are√3 apart; their section heights differ1. Thus tanδ=1/√3 and cosδ=√3/2.
The base area is3√3/2. Section area=(base projection)/cosδ.

problems.title: A cosine inequality with a missing input
problems.question: Solve cosx≥|x|/x.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: x=0 is undefined. For x<0 the right side is−1; for x>0 it is1.
steps: Every negative x works. Positive x work only when cosx=1, namely x=2πk,k=1,2,… .
problems.note: The closest printed option includes2πk for all integers, which accidentally includes the undefined value0. It needs that point removed.

problems.title: Two random arrivals and one-hour waiting
problems.question: Two people independently arrive uniformly between8 and10 and each waits1 hour. Find the meeting probability.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: They meet when the arrival-time difference is at most1.
steps: The sample square has area4. The two nonmeeting corner triangles each have area1/2.
Probability=1−1/4.

problems.title: A win given a player’s goal
problems.question: Bayern wins with probability.7,Barcelona with.3. A player scores with probabilities.9 and.6 conditional on those respective results. Given a goal, find P(Bayern win).
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Bayes numerator=.7·.9=.63; total goal probability=.63+.3·.6=.81.
steps: The conditional probability is.63/.81.

problems.title: A right triangular prism’s sphere center
problems.question: A right triangular prism has a right base angle C. A point is equally distant from all six vertices. On which face must it lie?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Its height is halfway between bases; its projection is the base circumcenter.
steps: For a right triangle, the circumcenter is midpoint of hypotenuse AB.
The spatial center is therefore the center of the rectangular face ABB₁A₁.

problems.title: A section-to-lateral-area ratio
problems.question: In a regular square pyramid, the section containing an apothem and the pyramid altitude has area one eighth of lateral area. Find the base dihedral.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: For base side a,height h,apothem l: section area=ah/2; lateral area=2al.
steps: ah/2=(2al)/8 implies h/l=1/2.
In the normal face triangle,sinδ=h/l.

problems.title: Three decreasing arithmetic binomial terms
problems.question: In(α+1)⁸, terms T₀,T₁,T₂ form a decreasing arithmetic progression. Which listed α works?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: Terms areα⁸,8α⁷,28α⁶. Arithmetic condition givesα⁶(α²−16α+28)=0.
steps: α=0 gives equal zero terms, not decreasing. The quadratic roots are2 and14.
At2, the terms increase; at14 they decrease because8/14<1 and(28/8)/14<1.

problems.title: Five-digit numbers with two digit-sum conditions
problems.question: How many five-digit numbers have first two digits summing to6 and last two summing to15?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: There are6 first pairs with nonzero leading digit,4 final pairs, and10 middle digits.
steps: First pairs are(1,5) through(6,0); final pairs are(6,9),(7,8),(8,7),(9,6).
Multiply independent choices:6·10·4.

problems.title: Equivalent equation and radical inequality
problems.question: Which listed a makes |x−2|=(a²−4)x²+3a equivalent to √(x²−4x+3)≤a(x+2)+2x?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: At a=−2,the equation is|x−2|=−6 and the inequality has right side−4.
steps: Neither can have a real solution because an absolute value or defined square root is nonnegative.
Thus their solution sets are both empty.

problems.title: A false set relation among prism classes
problems.question: A=prisms,B=right prisms,C=regular prisms,D=parallelepipeds,E=right parallelepipeds,F=rectangular boxes,G=cubes. Which listed relation is false?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: A regular prism is a right prism with a regular polygon base; its height need not equal a base side.
steps: Thus C∩F is the set of square-based right prisms, including heights different from their base side.
For example a1×1×2 box is in C∩F but is not a cube.

problems.title: Complete a valid line-plane implication
problems.question: A line is not contained in a plane. Which listed words make the statement “if it is … to … line(s) in the plane, then it is … to the plane” true?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: A line parallel to one line in a plane and not contained in that plane is parallel to the plane.
steps: If it intersected the plane, the parallel line through the intersection would lie entirely in the plane, forcing the original line to be contained too.
The contradiction proves parallelism. Perpendicularity to two unspecified lines is insufficient when those two are parallel.

problems.title: Sum the first ten positive trigonometric roots
problems.question: Find the sum of the least ten positive roots of tan²(2x)+1=sin²x.
problems.idea: Both sides can agree only at their common bound1.
formulas: tan²(2x)+1≥1 and sin²x≤1.
steps: Equality requires sin²x=1,so x=π/2+πk. At every such point,tan2x=0,so these and only these are roots.
The first ten positive roots areπ/2,3π/2,…,19π/2.

problems.title: A composed quadratic inequality valid everywhere
problems.question: f(x)=2sinx+1. Find a for which[f(x)]²−2af(x)+6a−9≤0 for every real x.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: t=f(x) ranges over[−1,3]. The quadratic in t is convex, so its maximum on that interval is at an endpoint.
steps: At t=3 the expression is0; at t=−1 it is8a−8.
Both are nonpositive exactly when a≤1.

problems.title: Count a trigonometric lattice inside a square
problems.question: Count pairs with cos(x+y)=cos(x−y)=1 and0<x<10,0<y<10.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: x+y=2πm,x−y=2πn,so x=π(m+n),y=π(m−n).
steps: The positive integers x/π,y/π can be1,2,3 and must have the same parity.
Odd-odd pairs give4 possibilities; even-even gives1.

problems.title: A pyramid with five equal edges
problems.question: A pyramid has rectangular base whose diagonals make60°. At least five pyramid edges are equal. Find the smallest face angle at the apex.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: The rectangle side ratio is1:√3. Its four lateral edges must be equal to the longer base side: three equal apex distances already force the fourth for a rectangle.
steps: Let longer side be l and shorter l/√3. Equal lateral edges cannot equal the shorter side, since that would place the apex at base circumradius l/√3 and zero height.
For equal lateral edges l, the apex angle opposite a short side has cosine[2l²−l²/3]/(2l²)=5/6.
The angle opposite the longer base side is60°, so the short-side apex angle is smaller.

problems.title: A line with equal images under scaling and translation
problems.question: Scaling by2 about the origin and translation by(−1,4) send which listed line to the same image line?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: For y=mx+b,scaling gives intercept2b; translation gives intercept b+4+m.
steps: Equal image lines require2b=b+4+m,so b=m+4.
Among the listed lines,y=3x+7 satisfies this condition.

problems.title: Length of a square-root solution set
problems.question: What is the length of the solution interval of √(2−x²)≥x?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: The domain is[−√2,√2]. Negative x satisfy the inequality automatically.
steps: For x≥0,square to get2−x²≥x²,so x≤1.
The full set is[−√2,1], with length1+√2.

problems.title: An equality that is impossible for all angles
problems.question: Which listed expression can never equal sin(α+β)?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: 1+tan²s≥1,where s=α+β. Equality with sins≤1 would require both sins=1 and tans=0.
steps: These requirements are incompatible; at sins=1,tan is in fact undefined.
The other listed expressions can match for suitable angles; for instance1+cot²s matches at s=π/2, and1−sins matches when sins=1/2.

problems.title: Choose a solution of a cosine inequality
problems.question: Which listed angle satisfies cosx<−0.2?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: cos(π−θ)=−cosθ.
steps: For x=π−arccos0.3,the cosine is−0.3<−0.2.
The other listed angles have cosines±0.1 or+0.3.

problems.title: Three coplanar box vectors
problems.question: In a rectangular box,AB=3,AD=5,AA₁=9. Which listed triple is coplanar?
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
steps: AB₁−BC₁=DB,so these three vectors are linearly dependent.
Their span has dimension at most2,which is precisely coplanarity for vectors.

problems.title: A zero scalar triple product
problems.question: For the same3×5×9 box,find(AB₁×BC₁)·DB.
problems.idea: Reduce the question using the rule below, then check the allowed values.
formulas: DB=AB₁−BC₁. A cross product is perpendicular to both factors.
steps: Dotting AB₁×BC₁ with either AB₁ or BC₁ gives0.
By linearity,dotting with their difference also gives0.
